chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa' from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Hasan ibn al-Mughira that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
The superiority of the supplication after the Obligatory (prayer) over the supplication after the optional (prayer) is like the superiority of the Obligatory (prayer) over the optional (prayer).
He said, then he said: 'Supplicate to Him and do not say that the matter is finished, for the supplication is the worship.'
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Surely those who are too proud to worship Me shall soon enter Hell abased.'
And He said: 'Call upon Me, I will Answer you.'

And he said: 'Whenever you intend to supplicate to Allah, so glorify Him, praise Him, declare His holiness, laud Him, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then ask, you will be given.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette and merit of supplication after prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish the primacy of post-obligatory supplication (du'a) as a continuation of the prayer ritual itself, distinguishing it from general voluntary acts. The Imam links this practice directly to the concept of 'ibadah (worship), warning against spiritual complacency ('qad furiga') by citing the Quranic warning against those who are too proud to worship. The prescribed etiquette of glorification and salawat serves as a spiritual preparation, ensuring the supplicant approaches God with humility and recognition of His majesty before making personal requests.
